newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil probes telecoms complaint against U.S. firm.
newsitem.headline: Brazil probes telecoms complaint against U.S. firm.

text.p: Brazil's Communications Ministry is investigating a complaint that U.S.-based McCaw International illegally entered the local telecoms market.

A ministry spokesman said Communications Minister Sergio Motta had received an anonymous complaint alleging that McCaw, under the name Airlink, was providing a mobile telephone "trunking" services without government authorization.
Company officials could not be reached for comment.
"We have a published list of 455 foreign companies and there is no company by that name," the ministry spokesman said, but he added: "The minister said he is very concerned. It is very serious."
According to a newspaper report, the complaint describes Airlink as Brazil's largest provider of "trunking" services with 1,700 frequencies, including 195 in Sao Paulo.
The reports said copies of the complaint were sent to the ministry, the media and consortia competing for concessions to operate in the B Band cellular frequency.
"Trunking" began as a radio system that evolved to include digital technology, which in turn allowed it to function like a highly sophisticated cellular phone system.

Daily Folha de S. Paulo said the company entered the local market through the purchase of local firms that had been granted frequency channels for free by the governments of former presidents Fernando Collor de Mello and Itamar Franco.
Under Brazilian law, the transfer of frequency licenses needs to be approved by the ministry.
